Also apply the lid mode on battery?

data.name: Welcome_Step1_Body
data.value:
KeepLid stops Windows from going to sleep while a long task runs: an AI agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor…), a build, a download, a render.
Click the icon next to the clock to turn it on or off. It turns off by itself after the chosen time, or when the process you picked ends. It never simulates keystrokes or mouse moves.

data.name: Welcome_Step2_Body
data.value:
To keep working with the lid closed, KeepLid temporarily sets “When I close the lid” to “Do nothing” — plugged in only, unless you also allow it on battery.
The original setting is saved first and restored automatically: when you turn KeepLid off, quit, sign out or shut down, and even after a crash, at the next launch.
If Windows does not allow apps to change this setting on your PC, KeepLid shows a step-by-step guide instead.

data.name: Welcome_Step3_Body
data.value:
With the lid closed, the built-in screen turns off (that is hardware), but the PC keeps working and producing heat.
Never leave a running laptop in a closed bag or on a soft surface (bed, sofa). KeepLid turns off by itself when the battery gets low.

data.name: Guide_Intro
data.value: On this PC, Windows only lets administrators change the power plan, and KeepLid never asks for administrator rights. You can change the lid setting yourself in 30 seconds:

data.name: Guide_Step2
data.value: 2. Next to “When I close the lid”, in the “Plugged in” column, choose “Do nothing”, then click “Save changes”.

data.name: Guide_Step3
data.value: 3. When your task is finished, set it back to “Sleep”. KeepLid reminds you when it turns off.
